long_biography.plain_text:
Software entrepreneur Gunther Thies initially wanted a business that could survive. He and his co-founder began without a business plan, then set their sights on making Winsolvenz a standard tool for insolvency administrators. Neither was a lawyer or computer scientist; they relied on a small specialist team whose early members remained in senior positions.

As STP grew, Thies sought to reduce dependence on one product and one customer market. He pursued additional business lines while giving employees considerable autonomy within narrowly chosen markets. He later moved to the supervisory board, reducing his workload with the intention of spending more time helping other entrepreneurs shape their businesses.
